photos.title: The Nile Valley and Delta From Space
photos.caption: NASA satellite view showing the narrow green ribbon of farmland along the Nile opening into the broad green Delta, walled on both sides by tan desert.
photos.creator: MODIS Land Rapid Response Team, NASA Goddard Space Flight Center
photos.credit: MODIS Land Rapid Response Team, NASA GSFC (Public Domain)

photos.title: The Narmer Palette (c. 3100 BCE)
photos.caption: Both faces of the two-foot-tall dark green siltstone carving from Hierakonpolis, showing King Narmer wearing the White Crown of the south (left) and the Red Crown of the north (right).
photos.creator: Unknown ancient Egyptian carver (photograph via Wikimedia Commons)
photos.credit: Egyptian Museum, Cairo (JE 32169 / CG 14716), via Wikimedia Commons (Public Domain)

photos.title: The Great Pyramid of Giza Today
photos.caption: Sunlit courses of rough yellow inner limestone blocks stacked 481 feet high around 2560 BCE; notice the tiny visitors along the base for scale. Smooth white outer casing stone was later stripped away.
photos.creator: Nina (Wikimedia Commons)
photos.credit: Photo by Nina, 2005, via Wikimedia Commons (CC BY 2.5)

photos.title: Model Egyptian Bakery and Brewery (c. 1981–1975 BCE)
photos.caption: A carved wooden workshop model placed in a noble's tomb about 600 years after Giza, showing how Egyptian bakers ground grain and shaped bread side by side with brewers filling beer jars.
photos.creator: Metropolitan Museum of Art
photos.institution: Metropolitan Museum of Art, New York
photos.credit: Metropolitan Museum of Art, Acc. 20.3.12, Rogers Fund and Edward S. Harkness Gift, 1920 (Open Access, CC0 1.0)

photos.title: Fresh Papyrus Reeds
photos.caption: Tall triangular marsh stalks (Cyperus papyrus) were sliced into thin strips, overlapped in criss-cross layers, and pressed flat into light paper-like scrolls for river logbooks and tax records.
photos.creator: Cayambe
photos.credit: Photo by Cayambe, 2024, via Wikimedia Commons (CC BY 4.0)

photos.title: Ancient Egyptian Scribe's Palette (c. 2030–1550 BCE)
photos.caption: A portable wooden writing board with two round ink wells—black soot ink for daily entries and red mineral ink for headings and totals—plus a slot holding reed brushes.
photos.creator: Metropolitan Museum of Art
photos.institution: Metropolitan Museum of Art, New York
photos.credit: Metropolitan Museum of Art, Acc. 10.176.62, Rogers Fund, 1910 (Open Access, CC0 1.0)

photos.title: Imhotep's Step Pyramid at Saqqara (c. 2670 BCE)
photos.caption: Six shrinking tiers of cut limestone rising 205 feet high—Egypt's first giant stone monument, built about a century before Khufu. Tiny visitors walk on the right for scale.
photos.creator: Vyacheslav Argenberg
photos.credit: Photo by Vyacheslav Argenberg, via Wikimedia Commons (CC BY 4.0)

photos.title: Sneferu's Bent Pyramid at Dahshur (c. 2600 BCE)
photos.caption: When soft clay-and-sand ground shifted mid-build, builders flattened the slope from 54 degrees to 43 degrees halfway up. Large patches of its original smooth white limestone casing still cling to the sides.
photos.creator: Jorge Láscar
photos.credit: Photo by Jorge Láscar, via Wikimedia Commons (CC BY 2.0)

photos.title: White Tura Casing Block From Khufu's Pyramid (c. 2560 BCE)
photos.caption: An original outer limestone block from the Great Pyramid, cut precisely to the 51.8-degree slope so neighboring stones locked together with seams narrower than a fingernail.
photos.creator: CaptMondo
photos.credit: British Museum, London; photo by CaptMondo via Wikimedia Commons (CC BY 2.5)

photos.title: Aswan Red Granite Quarry
photos.caption: More than 500 miles south of Giza, Egyptian quarrymen pounded giant beams straight out of hard pink-red granite bedrock using dolerite pounding stones, then floated them north on the Nile.
photos.creator: Glenn Ashton
photos.credit: Photo by Glenn Ashton, via Wikimedia Commons (CC BY-SA 3.0)

photos.title: Hauling a Giant Stone Statue on a Wooden Sledge (c. 1880 BCE)
photos.caption: Facsimile of a tomb wall painting at Deir el-Bersha showing 172 haulers in four rows dragging a massive seated statue on a runner sledge. Look closely right in front of the curved wooden runner: a small worker stands on the sledge pouring liquid onto the ground ahead.
photos.creator: Percy E. Newberry (1895 facsimile after ancient Egyptian tomb painting)
photos.institution: Tomb of Djehutihotep, Deir el-Bersha (published in El Bersheh, Part I, 1895)
photos.credit: Percy E. Newberry, El Bersheh, Part I (1895), via University of Heidelberg / Wikimedia Commons (Public Domain)

photos.title: Painted Offering Chapel of Perneb (c. 2381–2323 BCE)
photos.caption: Carved lines of bearers march toward a tomb's false door bringing bread, meat, and drink—showing how tax-free farming estates funded daily tomb offerings generation after generation.
photos.creator: Metropolitan Museum of Art
photos.institution: Metropolitan Museum of Art, New York
photos.credit: Metropolitan Museum of Art, Acc. 13.183.3, Gift of Edward S. Harkness, 1913 (Open Access, CC0 1.0)

photos.title: Early Egyptian Copper Chisel (c. 2650 BCE)
photos.caption: From Abydos near the dawn of Egypt's stone-pyramid age: hammered copper could shape softer limestone, yet blunted fast and could not cut hard granite until metalworkers alloyed copper with tin to make bronze.
photos.creator: Metropolitan Museum of Art
photos.institution: Metropolitan Museum of Art, New York
photos.credit: Metropolitan Museum of Art, Acc. 01.4.37, Gift of Egypt Exploration Fund, 1901 (Open Access, CC0 1.0)
